items.stem: Who is essential for a credible DITL interview?

options.text: Only someone who has never seen the workflow.
Only a generic industry report.
A representative person who actually does the prioritized work.
Only the certificate administrator.

items.stem: How should active effort and elapsed waiting be recorded?

options.text: Ignored because only screen count matters.
Both automatically multiplied by every employee's salary.
Added together and called removable labor.
Separately, with units, evidence status and the relevant business consequence.

items.stem: A 30-minute search and a two-day approval wait are reported. Which modeling approach is best?

options.text: Model search as active effort and waiting as cycle delay, with separate causal assumptions.
Treat the full two days as paid labor saved per case.
Ignore both because neither is useful evidence.
Assume the wait disappears without process change.

items.stem: Which future-state map is most defensible?

options.text: All approval controls are removed to maximize ROI.
Grounded retrieval/drafting with human review, exceptions and stated data dependencies.
Every current step becomes zero minutes automatically.
A diagram with unsupported write actions and no owners.
Never, even when the future state is disputed.
Only after the customer has fully deployed.
Always as an extra meeting with no objective.
When it resolves a specific workflow, feasibility or alignment uncertainty.
Only a product feature list.
Every click shown with no business consequence.
Outcome, pain, future change, evidence, metric plan and unresolved dependencies.
An unqualified savings percentage.

items.stem: Two interviews give very different task times. What is the best response?

options.text: Investigate persona/workflow differences and present a supported range or separate models.
Keep only the faster estimate to improve the story.
Average them blindly and claim precision.
Treat both as guaranteed measured baselines.

items.stem: The AI DITL generator invents exact step durations. What should the learner do?

options.text: Present them as stopwatch measurements.
Mark them unverified and obtain customer evidence before modeling.
Remove citations so the estimates cannot be challenged.
Use them because precision implies accuracy.
